content.intro: This lesson covers Variable Shadowing. It sits in Module 3, Rust Syntax and Primitive Data Types, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: Variable Shadowing matters when you work with language foundations. Understanding the rule helps you predict compiler or runtime behavior, document assumptions, and choose a safer implementation when inputs or system conditions change.

content_blocks.text: Variable Shadowing is one building block of this area: Read Rust syntax and use bindings, scalar types, numeric conversions, and formatting safely. Start with the smallest example, identify the inputs and assumptions, and check the edge cases before using the technique in a larger program.

content_blocks.title: A reliable way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: For Variable Shadowing, write down the inputs, the guarantee you expect, and the boundary where that guarantee stops. Work through a minimal example first; then deliberately test one edge case. Bindings are immutable unless declared mut; shadowing creates a new binding. Prefer explicit conversions and clear formatting over silently assuming a numeric conversion is safe.

content_blocks.text: Do not assume Variable Shadowing guarantees more than it actually does. Reduce a failure to a small reproducer, read the full compiler diagnostic or error value, consult the matching official reference, and change one assumption at a time.
